about: Did-provider confine falsifiers merged by tasks 001, 007, 009, 015, 019, 022 and 023, each anchored in the committed source. DID01 restores a temp-directory fallback for a missing or empty storage root, DID02 drops the absolute-path check, DID03 swallows a nickname read error, which both its unit test and the confinement's `outside_read_denied` catch, DID04 replaces `(deny default)` with `(allow default)`, DID05 grants the network, DID06 makes `verify_did_recovery` panic on a bad signature instead of returning a refusal, DID07 drops the process-exec grant, DID08 the root-directory read, DID09 the kernel-fact read, DID10 the storage-root state grant. Task 019 adds DID11, which returns `parse_error` instead of the non-hex signature refusal. Task 022 adds DID12 for a failure message that drops the child's standard error, DID13 for a spawn that drops the stderr pipe instead of draining it, DID14 for a failure message that omits the request, DID15 for one that omits the exit status, and DID16/DID17 for the failed-write and response-stream branches bypassing the shared diagnostic. Task 023 adds DID18, which widens the one write grant from `STORAGE_ROOT` to `STORAGE_PARENT`, so `outside_write_denied` fails on its sibling target because that write succeeds. Task 015 removed every other allow form from the profile because no confinement test needed it; the shared `STORAGE_PARENT` grant stays only for the one file-profile contract, and its removal falsifier is WP11 in `../wallet-provider/falsifiers.json`. A falsifier counts as caught only when every named test fails. Edit paths are relative to `examples/agent-host`, the one runner's rule, so every file starts with `../../`, and every edit snippet is verbatim in the current source. Task 031 adds DID19, which resolves edit paths from the repository root again: `tests::falsifiers_list_is_honest` fails on DID01 because the committed `../../` path no longer resolves, and `tests::falsifiers_list_rejects_a_repository_relative_path` fails because the DID01 refusal does not come. Task 027 adds DID20, which returns `Ok(false)` from the sandbox gate's declared-OS branch, so a missing `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` on macOS skips and passes; `sandbox_gate_fails_instead_of_skipping_on_a_declared_os` fails on its `macos` case. Run `python3 -I examples/agent-host/falsify.py --from capsules/did-provider/falsifiers.json` from the repository root, and the sandbox entries make the full run a Mac gate. Task 028 adds DID21, which starts the provider binary directly when its profile file does not exist, so the launch never applies the profile and `startup_is_refused_when_the_profile_cannot_be_applied` fails on its missing-profile case. Task 049 adds DID22, which returns `false` from the error arm of `sandbox_available`, so a missing `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` on macOS returns and the test passes; `sandbox_available_fails_for_macos_when_sandbox_exec_is_missing` fails. Task 052 adds DID23, which starts the stderr drainer only after the wait, so the fixture blocks on a full pipe and `stderr_is_drained_before_wait` fails on its exit assertion; DID24, which makes `unanswered` use a fixed `Operation not permitted` instead of the child's standard error, so `startup_denial_reports_its_reason` fails on its `execvp()` assertion; and DID25, which returns the shared unanswered message from the invalid-JSON branch, so `invalid_json_answer_names_the_request_and_the_parse_error` fails.
